title: Redesign rerank request/response ergonomics for deterministic defaults and rich structured output
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Replace the current ad-hoc rerank input/output shape with an ergonomic, backwards-compatible schema that: 1) makes 'k' semantics explicit and predictable for developers, 2) returns rich structured signals per candidate (scores, provenance, token-level spans), and 3) supports efficient pagination and low-latency bulk reranking. This ticket covers API shape decisions, default behaviors, and a migration path to avoid breaking existing customers.
acceptance_criteria: New request schema accepted by SDKs and Console (examples + tests included)
Server implements explicit 'k' (integer) and optional 'threshold' (float) + 'top_percent' (float) knobs and documents deterministic tie-breaking rules
Response contains per-candidate structured fields: normalized_score, raw_score, provenance_id, token_spans (when available), and tie_break_hint
Opaque pagination token supported for stable offsets across updates; cursor-less page offsets also available for low-latency clients
E2E perf tests: 99th percentile latency for 50-candidate rerank under target model remains <= 120ms in hosted environment
Migration guide published with example automatic translation of old parameters to new schema
migration_plan: Phase 1: Add new optional request fields (k, threshold, top_percent, stable_sort, tie_break_policy) behind feature flag
Phase 2: SDK patch release exposing new fields and example helpers to compute sensible defaults
Phase 3: Monitor usage for 4 weeks; provide opt-in conversion tool in Console to preview results
Phase 4: After deprecation window (90 days), change server default behavior to new ergonomic defaults and announce final removal of legacy shims
implementation_notes: Server: accept both legacy body and new unified 'input' array where each item may include precomputed embedding or raw text; prioritize precomputed embedding when present
Score normalization: transform model logits to a 0..1 normalized_score per-request using softmax over candidates to make thresholds meaningful
Determinism: stable_sort boolean defaults to true. tie_break_policy options: 'input_order', 'score_then_input', 'provenance_priority'. Implement a deterministic hashing fallback for identical scores
Pagination: produce opaque 'page_token' that encodes model_version + input_hash + offset + stability_vector. Also support fast 'offset' param for clients that prefer stateless pages

Structured output: include provenance_id (source URI or doc id), snippet (trimmed candidate), token_spans (start_token, end_token) when tokenizer available, and debug_flags when request includes debug=true
Batching: support server-side micro-batching of rerank scoring when many inputs are included; ensure KV cache reuse for repeated queries within same request to reduce tokenization/embedding costs
Telemetry: emit per-request top_k, top_percent, used_threshold, model_version, latency_ms, and memory_peak to the console for cost breakdowns
api_examples: Example new request (precomputed embeddings preferred): {"model":"rerank-a1","input":[{"id":"q-123","query":"How to rotate SSH keys?","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"Rotate keys with ssh-keygen...","embedding":null},{"id":"c2","text":"Manual rotation steps...","embedding":null}] }],"k":5,"stable_sort":true,"debug":false }
Backward-compat sample: server accepts legacy body with 'top_k' and maps to new 'k' with warning header 'X-Rerank-Deprecated: true'
